text.arabic_uthmani: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُم بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًۭا وَرُفَٰتًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًۭا جَدِيدًا

words.gloss_range: that; distant demonstrative pointing back to the punishment scene as the verdict now identified
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) begins with a pointed verdict rather than a new description. The demonstrative reaches back to the punishment scene in 17:97 and turns that scene into the identified recompense; its distance marker makes the prior image formally present, while its address element brings that distant referent into the verdict frame. Because the verdict comes before the causal explanation, the reader hears the sentence first classify the punishment and only then disclose the grounds.

topics.headline: distant demonstrative resumes the prior punishment scene (17:97)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the opening word point back to 17:97 and make that earlier punishment the specific referent of the verdict.
topics.reason: The QAC row and attachment cross-reference both identify the prior punishment scene (17:97) as the referent.

topics.headline: the demonstrative form carries distance and address together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pointing is not vague; distance and address combine in the form that opens the verdict.
topics.reason: The local demonstrative is compatible with the row family describing deictic force.

topics.headline: the ayah opens as nominal judicial summary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the movement from vivid punishment to a cooled nominal sentence that pronounces what that punishment is.
topics.reason: The word stands as the subject of a nominal predication before the causal clause arrives.

words.gloss_range: their recompense; a nominative verbal noun predicate naming the prior punishment as a matched return
words.root_gloss_range: recompensing, repaying, settling what is due; locally selected as matched return or recompense
words.prose: {{ar:جَزَآؤُهُم}} ({{tr:jazāʾuhum}}) names the prior punishment as their recompense, not as an unrelated event still waiting to happen. The verbal noun makes requital a stable judicial category, while the attached plural pronoun keeps the punished group bound to the return generated by their own acts. Its root pressure is matched repayment or account-settlement, so the following cause-clause reads like evidence explaining why this recompense belongs to them; that evidence includes their quoted speech, and the wording also recalls the surah's earlier recompense-with-Jahannam pattern (17:63).

topics.headline: recompense is the predicate identity of the sentence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment identified as recompense before any reason is argued.
topics.reason: The word is the nominative predicate of the demonstrative nominal sentence.

topics.headline: the attached pronoun makes recompense relational
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the recompense as a return tied to this group, whether foregrounding recipients or affected objects.
topics.reason: The suffix is locally licensed as the group receiving or undergoing the recompense.

topics.headline: the root frames punishment as balanced repayment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the verdict as an account being settled over their denial, not as arbitrary suffering.
topics.reason: The root range of recompense and due return coheres with the causal indictment.

topics.headline: recompense is tied to denial speech and the 17:63 formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees their quoted speech become part of the evidence for a familiar surah-local recompense pattern (17:63).
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete links between recompense, denial, speech, and the 17:63 formula.

words.gloss_range: causal preposition introducing the grounds for the verdict
words.prose: The first {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) turns the explanation into cause. It governs the asserted clause that follows, so the denial of signs and the quoted objection are not loose narrative additions; they are the grounds for the verdict. The repeated particle later has a different job, which makes this first occurrence the gateway from sentence to evidence.

topics.headline: causal preposition governs the whole indictment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from verdict to grounds through a single causal particle.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following content the cause of the recompense.

topics.headline: the particle and subordinator form a compact causal gateway
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical density: preposition plus subordinator compress the legal reason into one governed unit.
topics.reason: The local construction supports causal subordination into an asserted clause.

topics.headline: the first occurrence contrasts with the later object-marking occurrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes cause-marking from object-domain marking instead of flattening both particles into one vague force.
topics.reason: The ayah contains two local occurrences with different syntactic relations.

words.gloss_range: emphatic subordinator making the causal reason an asserted fact-clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) makes the reason an asserted fact-clause inside the causal phrase. It governs the pronoun subject and the denial predicate, so the charge is not presented as speculation. The particle also carries emphasis, fitting the legal feel of the ayah: the verdict is followed by a settled evidentiary statement.

topics.headline: the subordinator governs the causal fact-clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reason for recompense built as a full governed proposition.
topics.reason: The particle governs its subject and predicate inside the causal complement.

topics.headline: emphatic subordination turns the reason into legal evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the causal claim as settled evidence against denial, not a mere report.
topics.reason: The particle embeds and emphasizes the following content under the causal preposition.

words.gloss_range: they denied or covered; completed collective denial directed through a bi-complement at divine signs
words.root_gloss_range: covering, denying, rejecting, and ingratitude; locally denial/covering of divine signs through a bi-complement
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) records the first charge as a completed collective act. In this frame the verb reaches its target through the following preposition, so the denial is aimed at a specified domain of divine signs. The root image of covering matters because signs are meant to be read; this is hostile concealment of evidence, not the remedial covering suggested by a different root-family derivative. The same plural ending then carries the group into their quoted new-creation objection, a pattern also visible in 13:5, while the surrounding context answers covering with exposed punishment before it (17:97) and creator-power response after it (17:99).

topics.headline: the perfect verb enters denial into the record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees denial as a completed deed now serving as grounds for recompense.
topics.reason: The perfect Form I verb supplies the predicate content of the asserted causal clause.

topics.headline: denial is directed through a prepositional complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act is not generic unbelief; it is denial aimed at the sign-domain.
topics.reason: The next preposition governs the signs as the object-domain of the verb.

topics.headline: covering-denial opposes readable evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears moral blame and epistemic refusal together: they cover what should have functioned as signs.
topics.reason: The covering-denial sense fits the local complement naming signs.

topics.headline: a remedial-covering derivative sharpens the hostile local act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can contrast hostile covering of signs with a different remedial covering branch, while the local verb remains denial.
topics.reason: The derivative contrast is valid root-family pressure but does not replace the selected local sense.

topics.headline: the same plural group denies and then speaks
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one plural subject carry both the denial of signs and the quoted new-creation objection, including the parallel pattern in 13:5.
topics.reason: The plural suffix and conjoined speech clause bind the charges to the same group.

topics.headline: surrounding fire and creator-power answer the covering act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denial answered on both sides: exposed punishment before it and creator-power response after it (17:99).
topics.reason: The boundary rows coherently connect the local denial to the adjacent punishment (17:97) and response (17:99).

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the specific sign-domain targeted by the denial
words.prose: The second {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) does not repeat the causal work of the first one. Here it marks the domain against which the denial is directed, binding the sign phrase to the verb. The two occurrences together make the clause compact: recompense is because of denial, and denial is specifically against the signs.

topics.headline: the second preposition governs the denied signs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees exactly what their denial targets rather than treating the verb as free-floating disbelief.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies this occurrence as the preposition governing the sign phrase.

topics.headline: repeated particles create cause plus object architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compact legal chain: cause of verdict, then target of denial.
topics.reason: The two prepositions have separate local syntactic roles.

words.gloss_range: Our signs; divinely owned readable markers governed as the target-domain of denial
words.root_gloss_range: sign, mark, indication, verse; contested adjacent derivations do not replace the local sign-marker sense
words.prose: {{ar:ءَايَٰتِنَا}} ({{tr:āyātinā}}) names the denied object-domain as divine signs. Its plural construct and attached pronoun make the evidence both multiple and owned by the divine speaker, while the case shows it is governed by the preceding preposition. Because signs are readable markers, the charge is sharper than vague skepticism: they cover what was given to be recognized, and the sensory punishment in 17:97 answers that refusal by removing faculties for perceiving signs. A contested refuge-adjacent root pressure can remain only as secondary resonance, a refused return-point beside the local sign sense. The word also closes a surah sign arc from signs shown at the opening (17:1) to hostile sign-speech later in the surah (17:101).

topics.headline: case, plural, and suffix make the signs specified divine evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denied evidence as plural divine signs, not an undefined object.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the preposition and carries the attached divine pronoun.

topics.headline: signs are markers meant to be recognized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the collision between readable signs and the covering-denial named earlier.
topics.reason: The local complement makes the sign-marker sense central to the denial.

topics.headline: refused signs match the sensory deprivation in 17:97
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment scene of 17:97 answers refused signs with lost faculties for perceiving.
topics.reason: The boundary rows link signs to the immediately preceding sensory punishment scene (17:97).

topics.headline: contested refuge adjacency does not replace the sign sense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps a small path/refuge resonance while reading the local noun as signs governed by denial.
topics.reason: The valid dispute is retained only as pressure because local grammar and alignment select the sign noun.

topics.headline: the sign noun belongs to the 17:1 and 17:101 sign chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this denial of signs with the surah opening display of signs (17:1) and the later sign exchange (17:101).
topics.reason: The row family gives concrete surah-local sign references (17:1; 17:101).

words.gloss_range: and; conjunction adding their quoted speech as a second causal charge
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds a second count to the indictment. It coordinates their saying with their denial, so the direct quote is not ornamental; it is part of the causal evidence explaining the recompense. The prefixed conjunction makes the transition into speech tight and visible.

topics.headline: coordination adds quoted speech to denial as a charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees their words counted alongside their denial as grounds for the sentence.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the speech verb with the denial verb inside the causal content.

words.gloss_range: they said; completed collective speech introducing the direct resurrection-denial quote
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speaking, declaring; locally a completed collective speech act introducing direct quotation
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) turns the indictment into quoted evidence. The perfect plural verb records a completed collective utterance, and the direct quote that follows lets their own words specify the denial already named. Its plural ending matches the earlier denial verb, so the deniers and speakers are the same accused group. The same speech-report pattern also recalls the earlier resurrection objection in 17:49 and broader rebellious speech in 17:61-62, so the saying is not neutral narration.

topics.headline: the speech verb opens a direct evidentiary quotation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the denial in the speakers’ own recorded words rather than as narrator summary.
topics.reason: The following words form the quoted complement of the speech verb.

topics.headline: their saying becomes legal evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees speech itself become material for the verdict.
topics.reason: The verb is coordinated with the denial as part of the causal indictment.

topics.headline: plural morphology matches the earlier denial verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one accused group through denial and speech.
topics.reason: Both verbs are third-person plural perfect forms linked by coordination.

topics.headline: the speech verb reprises objections in 17:49 and 17:61-62
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the quote as part of the surah’s recurring speech of refusal, including 17:49 and 17:61-62.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete same-surah speech parallels (17:49; 17:61-62).

words.gloss_range: interrogative plus temporal condition, opening an incredulous future protasis
words.prose: {{ar:أَإِذَا}} ({{tr:a-idhā}}) opens the quoted objection by making a future condition sound incredulous. The temporal particle with the perfect verb projects a completed state of decomposition, while the interrogative force bends that condition into denial rather than information-seeking. The hamza variants expose the pressure point by easing, lengthening, or omitting the explicit question onset, and the canonical opening still begins with a catch of disbelief. As in the repeated wording from 17:49, this condition waits for the emphatic apodosis rather than standing as a loose question.

topics.headline: question plus temporal condition opens the denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the speakers turn a future condition into a challenge: when this has happened, then can raising occur?
topics.reason: The word supplies the temporal interrogative frame for the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: hamza variants and sound mark recitational pressure without changing local force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audible difficulty at the start of disbelief, while canonical question force remains the local reading.
topics.reason: The accepted variants clarify audible pressure but do not replace the local canonical construction.

topics.headline: the protasis belongs to the repeated 17:49 double-question formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the condition as the first half of a denial architecture reprising the same wording from 17:49.
topics.reason: The row family connects this opening condition to the following emphatic question and to 17:49.

words.gloss_range: we were or will have become; copular perfect under the temporal condition, requiring predicate complements
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing in a state or position; locally copular becoming within a conditional quote
words.prose: {{ar:كُنَّا}} ({{tr:kunnā}}) makes the speakers imagine themselves as having become the decomposed predicates that follow. The verb is copular, so it requires those predicates rather than standing alone, and under the temporal condition its perfect form pictures decomposition as a completed future state. Its root-family place/state pressure makes that existence feel like taking up a position in the state of bones, while the first-person plural suffix pulls the accused group into their own quoted scenario. The same self-description reprises 17:49, and the nasal ending leads audibly into the following tanwīn decay terms.

topics.headline: the copular perfect requires decomposed predicates
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the quote describe a state of becoming, not a free action.
topics.reason: The following accusative nouns are predicate complements of the copula.

topics.headline: place/state pressure stays within copular becoming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel existence as position-in-state, while local grammar keeps the word as a copular verb.
topics.reason: The derivative pressure is coherent but subordinated to the local copular construction.

topics.headline: the suffix makes the speakers the imagined decomposed subjects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reported group become the quote’s own we.
topics.reason: The first-person plural suffix identifies the speakers inside the direct quotation.

topics.headline: the copular phrase belongs to the 17:49 resurrection-denial formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this becoming-into-remains phrase as a reprise of the earlier objection at 17:49.
topics.reason: The row family gives same-surah formula links (17:49).

topics.headline: the plural suffix leads into the decay cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the we-form feed into the repeated indefinite endings of the remains.
topics.reason: The sound observation is locally tied to the suffix and following tanwīn terms.

words.gloss_range: bones; indefinite accusative predicate state naming skeletal remains
words.root_gloss_range: bone and bodily structure, with broader greatness or mass associations narrowed here to skeletal remains
words.prose: {{ar:عِظَٰمًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿiẓāman}}) is the first material predicate of the imagined state: they picture themselves as bones. The accusative indefinite plural makes the remains generic and exposed, while the root’s broader greatness field is narrowed to the concrete skeletal noun. That narrowing still leaves a payoff: bones are the durable bodily framework, and the next decay term pushes even that framework toward disintegration. The objection is not unanswerable in the wider Quranic field, because 2:259 shows bones raised and clothed with flesh; here the same -an cadence begins a chain from bones to fragments to re-creation.

topics.headline: bones are an accusative predicate state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the speakers identify themselves with remains, not merely with possessions or objects near them.
topics.reason: The noun is the predicate complement of the copular verb.

topics.headline: root greatness pressure narrows to durable skeletal structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the load-bearing core image while reading the local noun as literal bones.
topics.reason: The broader root field is useful as pressure but the local word selects skeletal remains.

topics.headline: the bones motif has a concrete reanimation answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear this objection against the visible bone-reanimation scene of 2:259.
topics.reason: The row family gives a concrete cross-reference for bones being revived (2:259).

topics.headline: bones start the decay pair and tanwīn chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first remains-word begin a sequence that moves from bones to fragments to re-creation.
topics.reason: The noun is paired with the following decay term and shares the accusative indefinite cadence.

words.gloss_range: and; conjunction coordinating a second decomposed-state predicate
words.prose: The middle {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second remains-word with the first predicate. It does not let the second term collapse into a restatement; it keeps the two states paired while allowing escalation from skeletal remains to pulverized fragments. The visible prefix makes the turn into the harsher decay image compact.

topics.headline: the conjunction pairs two predicate states while marking escalation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees two coordinated states of decomposition, with the second intensifying the first.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence joins the second predicate state to the first.

words.gloss_range: and fragments; coordinated accusative predicate of pulverized remains
words.root_gloss_range: breaking, crushing, and scattered fragments; locally pulverized remains in the resurrection objection
words.prose: {{ar:وَرُفَٰتًا}} ({{tr:wa-rufātan}}) completes the imagined decomposition by moving past bones into pulverized remains. Its rarity and breakage-root pressure make the image more than ordinary dust: the speakers choose a word for form-erasure, with a rough consonantal texture suited to crumbling matter. The term repeats the rare decomposition word from 17:49 and becomes the hinge before the apodosis; from maximum fragmentation the quote turns to the possibility they deny, being raised as a new creation.

topics.headline: the word extends the copular complement as a second predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees fragments as the second predicate state, visibly joined to bones.
topics.reason: The noun is coordinated with the first predicate complement of the copular verb.

topics.headline: the rare noun names crushed formless remains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the denial press the body to apparent information loss and form-erasure.
topics.reason: The lexical rows and contextual rarity support a marked pulverized-remains sense.

topics.headline: fragments face the new-creation phrase across the quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rare fragment word return from 17:49 and stand opposite the closing new-creation claim.
topics.reason: The row family ties this word to the same-surah formula (17:49) and to the later creation phrase in this ayah.

topics.headline: some rows press the following question, with this word as hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the fragment word as the end of the protasis before the quote shifts into the emphatic resurrection challenge.
topics.reason: The rows concern the following interrogative-emphatic clause, so their payoff is narrowed to how this word closes the condition before that clause.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle in the quoted apodosis, governing the speaker subject and predicate
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) begins the quoted apodosis with assertion-strength inside an incredulous question. It governs the speaker subject and the raised predicate, so the clause is grammatically strong even while the speech act uses that strength to deny. This is the first part of the emphatic stack that makes the rejected resurrection claim sound deliberately heightened, and it answers the bones-and-fragments condition while joining the surah's b-ʿ-th dispute pattern about sending in 17:94 and raising here.

topics.headline: the particle governs the quoted apodosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the resurrection claim shaped as a governed emphatic clause, not a loose phrase.
topics.reason: The particle governs the pronoun subject and predicate in the apodosis.

topics.headline: assertion and interrogation remain active together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the irony: the speakers quote the claim in strong assertion-form while using it as denial.
topics.reason: The preceding interrogative frame bends the emphatic clause into incredulous speech.

topics.headline: the emphatic clause answers the decay condition and joins the 17:94 dispute pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the apodosis answer the bones-and-fragments condition while linking resurrection denial to the sending objection in 17:94.
topics.reason: The rows identify both the local condition-apodosis relation and the same-surah root contrast (17:94).

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām attached to the passive resurrection predicate
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la-}}) moves the emphasis onto the resurrection predicate itself. It is not a loose particle; it is bound to the word for being raised, so the pressure lands exactly where the speakers resist the claim. Together with the preceding emphatic particle and the question frame, it creates an overcharged denial rather than a calm affirmation.

topics.headline: the emphatic lām locks onto the passive predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that emphasis falls on being raised, not merely on the speakers.
topics.reason: The particle reinforces the predicate of the emphatic clause and is attached to the passive participle.

topics.headline: question, emphatic particle, and lām amplify the denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears maximal assertion-form being used as the shape of disbelief.
topics.reason: The lām participates in the local interrogative-emphatic stack.

words.gloss_range: ones raised; passive participle predicate for resurrection, suppressing the raiser while foregrounding the raised group
words.root_gloss_range: raising, rousing, sending, dispatching; locally passive resurrection raising with motion-from-inertness pressure
words.prose: {{ar:مَبْعُوثُونَ}} ({{tr:mabʿūthūna}}) is the predicate at the center of the challenge: the speakers ask whether they will be made raised ones. The passive participle makes them patients and leaves the raiser unnamed, even though the grammar still requires an agent. The root’s rousing and dispatch range gives resurrection motion-from-inertness pressure, but the local form narrows it to passive resurrection raising; the plural ending keeps the whole speaking group inside that raised status. The same passive predicate repeats the objection from 17:49, links resurrection denial with the sending objection in 17:94 and the denial pair in 11:7, and its guttural-fricative weight makes the contested raising term sound heavier than the surrounding particles.

topics.headline: passive participle suppresses the raiser and foregrounds patients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the speakers resist agency while their own grammar still requires someone to raise them.
topics.reason: The passive participle encodes patient status and omits the agent.

topics.headline: rousing and dispatch pressure narrows to resurrection raising
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the sense of being roused into motion while reading the local predicate as resurrection raising.
topics.reason: The broader root range is coherent as pressure, but local passive predicate and creation complement select resurrection.

topics.headline: plural participial ending ties raised status to the speaking group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole quoted we-group become the rational plural predicate.
topics.reason: The ending agrees with the first-person plural subject of the emphatic clause.

topics.headline: the predicate belongs to the 17:49, 17:94, and 11:7 resurrection dispute field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the passive raising predicate as disputed speech linked to 17:49, 17:94, and 11:7.
topics.reason: The row family supplies concrete same-surah and cross-surah parallels (17:49; 17:94; 11:7).

topics.headline: the resurrection word carries rough acoustic weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the contested raising term as heavier than the surrounding particles.
topics.reason: The sound observation is tied to the local consonants of the predicate.

words.gloss_range: creation or created state; accusative verbal noun specifying the mode or kind of being raised
words.root_gloss_range: creating, shaping, proportioning, and fabrication; locally creation/re-forming, with fabrication pressure only as quoted-word edge
words.prose: {{ar:خَلْقًۭا}} ({{tr:khalqan}}) specifies what kind or state of being raised is under challenge: raised as a new creation. Its accusative role can be heard as state or specification, and the verbal noun keeps the process of forming close to the resulting created state. The root’s shaping and cutting pressure answers the preceding fragments with re-formation, while the fabrication branch remains only a quoted-speech edge; the local phrase is about creation. The wording belongs to the new-creation challenge formula in passages such as 13:5, 17:49, 17:51, 32:10, 34:7, and 50:15, and its tanwīn continues the audible path from decay terms into re-forming.

topics.headline: the accusative noun qualifies the raising predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees resurrection specified as a mode or category of new creation, not merely as upward motion.
topics.reason: The noun describes the state or specification of the passive predicate.

topics.headline: creation and shaping answer fragmented matter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final phrase answer form-loss with skilled re-forming.
topics.reason: The shaping/creation sense coheres with the preceding bones and fragments.

topics.headline: fabrication sense pressures quoted denial but does not replace creation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a double edge in the speakers’ wording while keeping creation as the selected local sense.
topics.reason: The broader fabrication branch is retained as quoted-speech pressure, not as the local phrase meaning.

topics.headline: the verbal noun leaves act and created state close together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase names renewed forming itself, not only a counted object.
topics.reason: The form is a singular indefinite verbal noun in an accusative qualifying role.

topics.headline: the phrase belongs to resurrection challenge formulas such as 13:5 and 17:49
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this phrase to the recurring new-creation challenge, including 13:5, 17:49, 17:51, 32:10, 34:7, and 50:15.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete formula references and same-surah links (13:5; 17:49; 17:51; 32:10; 34:7; 50:15).

topics.headline: the accusative ending carries decay into re-creation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same ending move from remains to renewed forming.
topics.reason: The cadence row is locally tied to the sequence of indefinite accusatives.

words.gloss_range: new or fresh; accusative indefinite adjective locked to the creation noun
words.root_gloss_range: newness, freshness, renewal, and fresh-cut associations; locally an adjective modifying the creation noun
words.prose: {{ar:جَدِيدًا}} ({{tr:jadīdan}}) is the final adjective of the quote and the ayah. Agreement locks it to the creation noun, so newness qualifies the created state rather than floating over the whole predicate, and the indefinite form presents that new creation as an unbounded type or quality. Its fresh-cut pressure sharpens the image of newly formed creation after pulverization, not merely repaired matter. The word belongs to the marked new-creation formula across 13:5, 14:19, 17:49, 17:98, 32:10, 34:7, 35:16, and 50:15; as the final -an cadence after bones, fragments, and creation, it leaves the deniers’ speech hanging on the very possibility of renewal that the opening recompense judges.

topics.headline: case and indefiniteness lock newness to the creation noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees newness modify creation specifically, not the passive raising predicate by itself.
topics.reason: The adjective agrees with the preceding creation noun in case and indefiniteness.

topics.headline: fresh-cut root pressure sharpens adjective newness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels newness as freshly formed creation, while the local word remains a qualitative adjective.
topics.reason: The root-family pressure is valid but narrowed to the local adjective modifying creation.

topics.headline: indefinite adjective leaves new creation as an unbounded type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the phrase present a new created state rather than a named prior entity simply restored.

topics.headline: the adjective belongs to the recurring new-creation formula (13:5; 17:49)
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the closing adjective as part of a marked resurrection-dispute formula across 13:5, 14:19, 17:49, 17:98, 32:10, 34:7, 35:16, and 50:15.
topics.reason: The rows give the concrete formula distribution and the contextual profile supports the creation collocation.

topics.headline: closing newness loops back to opening recompense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the quote close on the denied possibility that explains why the opening verdict is due.
topics.reason: The adjective is the ayah-final word and is linked by the row family to the opening verdict.

topics.headline: newness reverses fragmentation and completes the cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees a movement from pulverized remains to fresh formedness within one quoted sentence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causal clause links recompense to rejection of the signs.
baseline_models.mechanism: The focus joins a return fitted to an act, obstruction of truth, and visible evidence. Recompense is therefore an answer to how evidence was handled, not an arbitrary destination.

activation_trace.role: Matching an act with its return supplies the clause's juridical hinge.
Blocking or denying truth names the act for which return is due.
A visible mark makes the rejected object evidence rather than an unsupported claim.

changed_reading.after: The recompense is functionally fitted to an act of blocking visible evidence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence moves from bones and debris through being raised to a new creation.
baseline_models.mechanism: Solid remainder is reduced to scattered matter; dormant matter is stirred, measured, creatively formed, and made to occur anew after a break. The question challenges the whole transition across material discontinuity.

activation_trace.role: Pulverization and scattered debris define the material discontinuity.
Stirring what is still or dormant supplies transition out of inertness.
Measurement before formation supplies ordering of the residue.
Creative bringing-forth supplies the actual formation.
Renewed occurrence after a break marks the endpoint as genuinely new.

changed_reading.before: The question asks whether the dead return.
changed_reading.after: The question asks whether dispersed residue can be reactivated, remeasured, and formed into a renewed configuration after rupture.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The deniers say the bones-and-fragments question aloud.
baseline_models.mechanism: Speech carries an adopted position, and fragmentation is selected as its premise. The interrogative operates as a counter-doctrine that rules creative renewal out, not merely as unformed private uncertainty.

activation_trace.role: Speech as adopted belief makes the question a professed position.
Fragmentation is selected as the premise of that position.
Creative bringing-forth is the possibility the position excludes.

changed_reading.after: Their utterance formulates a public counter-model in which fragmentation cancels the possibility of creative renewal.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding sensory sequence embodies rejection of signs as blocked seeing, speaking, and hearing. It makes the fitted recompense a bodily counterpart to failed reception.

activation_trace.role: A matching return licenses a reciprocal rather than merely adjacent relation.
Obstruction of truth supplies the chosen epistemic act.
Visible signs specify what their perception failed to receive.
Loss of sight supplies the visual counterpart to rejected signs.
Blocked speech answers the focus utterance with embodied inability to utter.
Failure of hearing completes the reciprocal closure of reception.

structural_cues: 17:97 immediately precedes the deictic opening of 17:98, and its face-blind-dumb-deaf sequence stands directly before the causal recompense clause.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rejected signs and three sensory incapacities; I infer reciprocal fitting between chosen non-reception and embodied incapacity. Alternatively, the sensory states may be punitive attributes without strict correspondence.

changed_reading.before: Recompense is a consequence attached to disbelief.
changed_reading.after: Recompense enacts the deniers' own closure to signs as a closure of embodied perception and expression.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding recurrence clause makes recompense dynamic: every abatement triggers added ignition. The return is not only a state but a self-renewing counteraction.

activation_trace.role: Fitted return lets the preceding recurrence define how the recompense operates.
Fire subsiding supplies the loop's detection condition.
Increase supplies the response that reverses abatement.
Ignition supplies the renewed output of the recurrence.

structural_cues: The 'whenever...we increase' construction in 17:97 is picked up by the deictic 'that' at the start of 17:98.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a recurrence in which subsiding fire is answered by increased blaze; I infer that this loop is part of the functional shape of recompense. Alternatively, recompense may denote the whole prior fate while the loop remains one detail.

changed_reading.before: The recompense is a fixed sentence.
changed_reading.after: The recompense behaves as an iterated feedback process in which every decline triggers renewed intensity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah answers the material objection with creative capacity, creation of their likeness, and a bounded term. Renewal can preserve a patterned identity even while the focus calls its resulting configuration new.

activation_trace.role: Creative bringing-forth is the operation whose mode the context sharpens.
New occurrence after rupture keeps discontinuity genuinely live.
Repeated creating scales the operation from cosmos to renewed humans.
Effective capacity shifts the issue from available matter to ability to act.
Likeness supplies patterned continuity without itself settling material sameness.
A fixed temporal limit turns speculative impossibility into a scheduled event.

structural_cues: 17:99 directly answers the focus interrogation with seeing, cosmic creation, capacity, likeness, and an appointed term.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies capacity to create their like and a fixed term; I infer that newness can preserve patterned identity without requiring reuse of identical matter. Alternatively, likeness may assert equivalent creative power while ordinary same-person resurrection remains intended.

changed_reading.before: Renewal means putting the same debris back together.
changed_reading.after: Renewal may be a new instantiation of preserved human pattern, with the exact basis of continuity left unresolved.

context_deltas.mechanism: Clear signs, acknowledged knowledge, and inward sight are met by a spoken magic-label. Rejection becomes an active rhetorical reclassification of evidence rather than a mere absence of evidence.

activation_trace.role: Blocking truth supplies the interpretive act sharpened by the later exchange.
Attributing an untrue account supplies speech's relabeling capacity.
The signs remain overt marks rather than absent data.
Manifest disclosure intensifies the evidence's visibility.
A claim framed as supposition introduces the counterlabel.
Diversion and deception supply the label used to neutralize the signs.
Knowledge as disclosure makes simple ignorance an inadequate model.
Inner sight characterizes the signs as instruments of discernment.
The mirrored formula can carry conviction from an indicator, exposing a contest over warranted judgment.

structural_cues: 17:101 places clear signs beside Pharaoh's accusation; 17:102 places 'you knew' and insights beside a mirrored emphatic judgment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies clarity, knowledge, inner sight, and a magic-label; I infer that denial works by relabeling recognized evidence. Alternatively, the assertion of Pharaoh's knowledge may be rhetorical rather than a report of his private certainty.

changed_reading.before: They fail to assent because the signs do not persuade them.
changed_reading.after: They preserve denial by redescribing manifest signs so that acknowledged evidence no longer governs their public conclusion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent revelation sequence combines stable truth, collection in recitation, differentiation into parts, interval, and progressive delivery. It supplies a cross-domain process image in which partition does not erase the whole and can support ordered reformation.

activation_trace.role: Scattered fragments pose the continuity problem.
Measured formation supplies an ordering operation on parts.
Renewed occurrence supplies the reconstituted endpoint.
Stable correspondence through descent supplies continuity across transmission.
Gathering supplies a whole that can coexist with differentiated delivery.
Separation into parts supplies the material analogy to fragmentation.
Waiting with stability makes ordered sequence, not instant assembly, viable.
Progressive delivery supplies controlled transfer of the differentiated whole.

structural_cues: In 17:106 differentiation is followed by reading over an interval and emphatic progressive descent, so separation and ordered coherence coexist.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a truth-bearing whole differentiated and delivered over time; I analogize that process to bodily fragments becoming ordered creation. The live alternative is that the revelation process has no intended material analogy to resurrection.

changed_reading.before: Fragmentation means continuity has been irretrievably erased.
changed_reading.after: Fragmentation can be heard as a state of parts awaiting ordered collection and formation, not proof that a coherent whole is impossible.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those who receive the recited signs repeatedly fall, prostrate, weep, and deepen in humility; the focus deniers ask whether they will be raised. Voluntary lowering now contrasts with eventual compulsory activation.

activation_trace.role: Signs are the common stimulus separating the two bodily responses.
Stirring the still supplies the future compulsory movement.
Audible falling supplies voluntary bodily descent before the signs.
Self-lowering gives the descent an ethical posture.
Repeated falling turns posture into a sustained response pattern.
Tears and voiced grief add affective yielding to physical descent.
Increase makes receptive response deepen rather than close.
Humility identifies the inward counterpart of the lowered body.

structural_cues: The falling-on-chins construction occurs in both 17:107 and 17:109, while the focus places signs beside the disputed future raising.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated voluntary descent in response to signs and the focus supplies future raising; I infer an ethical posture contrast. Alternatively, prostration may be only a positive response with no direct mechanism for reading resurrection.

changed_reading.before: Being raised is only a disputed physical event.
changed_reading.after: Compulsory raising also contrasts with the willing self-lowering already produced by receptive encounter with the signs.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries resource economy into a metaphysical objection. It remains anchored in the focus question about renewed creating and in the adjacent store-hold-spend-narrow sequence; render it only as a possible projection of human scarcity, not as an asserted doctrine.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The phrase about a new creation asks whether creative renewal remains available after apparent material loss.

activation_trace.role: Creative bringing-forth is the capacity being tacitly treated as exhaustible.
Renewal after rupture is what scarcity logic makes difficult to imagine.
Guarded stores supply the finite-reserve model.
Avaricious holding supplies the response to feared depletion.
Expenditure supplies the imagined drain on a reserve.
Narrowing and reduction characterize the projected human economy.

changed_reading.before: Denial is based only on matter's destruction.
changed_reading.after: The objection may project finite-store economics onto creative power: once matter is spent, renewed creation seems unaffordable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-scale analogy from bodily debris to dispersed people. It remains anchored in the focus's fragmentation-raising-creation sequence and is activated by gathering and mixed assembly in 17:103-104; render it as structural resonance, not as a replacement for bodily resurrection.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus sequences scattered remains, activation, and newly formed existence.

activation_trace.role: Scattered debris supplies the dispersed starting state.
Dispatch and direction supply collective mobilization.
Creative formation anchors the analogy back in the focus.
Joining what is dispersed supplies recomposition at the group scale.
Bringing and presenting supplies external agency in the assembly.
Mixed elements wrapped into one group supply the socially recomposed endpoint.

changed_reading.before: The question concerns only re-forming individual bodies.
changed_reading.after: The dispersion-recomposition pattern can also resonate socially: scattered or mixed peoples are brought as a newly assembled collective.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation is surprising because it uses a root-level greatness resonance while the focus surface still plainly denotes bones. It remains anchored in that bone term and the closing command to magnify; downstream prose must present it as rhetorical resonance, never as an alternative translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The bone term carries a root inventory that includes both solid bone and deeming something immense or daunting.

activation_trace.role: Solid bone is the literal residue made central to the objection.
Deeming a matter immense supplies a contained rhetorical resonance around that residue.
Magnifying something in the breast redirects perceived magnitude toward the final command's object.

changed_reading.before: Bones are neutral remains offered as evidence against renewal.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the deniers rhetorically enlarge the remains into an impossible obstacle, while the closing command redirects magnitude away from the obstacle.

strongest_changes: Recompense becomes an embodied and recursively renewed counterpart to rejected perception.
New creation is reframed through capacity, likeness, and a fixed term, leaving the exact basis of continuity open.
Clear signs plus asserted knowledge make disbelief look like active relabeling rather than missing evidence.
Differentiated revelation suggests, exploratorily, that partition can preserve an ordered whole.
summary.what_was_special: The deictic tie to 17:97 produced a feedback model, while repeated part-whole, rise-fall, and gathering patterns changed how the focus's material vocabulary functioned without collapsing the readings into one.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether likeness specifies the mode of personal continuity or only analogizes creative power.
Whether textual and social recomposition are intended mechanisms or only contextual resonances.
Whether the sensory incapacities are strict reciprocal counterparts or simply attributes of punishment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The earlier fragmentation objection returns as the causal pattern of sensory closure.** `ج ز ي:B001` matching return, `ك ف ر:B003` covers truth, `ء ي ي:B003` visible sign, `ر ف ت:B001` fragments, `ب ع ث:B001` rouses, and `ج د د:B004` newness. 17:49's speech is now quoted as explanation for 17:97's condition. I infer a material model that denies reassembly also covers the signs that would reorient perception. Recompense reads as cognition returned in embodied form.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:99 immediately answers the repeated material objection with visible cosmic origination. This confirms that the punishment's match lies in refused inference, not in asking about matter itself.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Matching recompense answers a fragmentation model that covered the signs.** Lexical evidence: `ج ز ي B001` (recompense matching an act) in `جَزَآؤُهُم`, `ك ف ر B003` (covering or rejecting truth) in `كَفَرُوا۟`, `ر ف ت B001` (breaking into scattered fragments) in `رُفَٰتًا`, `ب ع ث B001` (rousing a still thing into motion) in `مَبْعُوثُونَ`, `خ ل ق B001` (measuring and proportioning) in `خَلْقًا`, and `ج د د B004` (newness after cutting) in `جَدِيدًا`. Structural cue: 17:97 embodies blocked channels and gathering, this ayah names denial as cause, and 17:99 answers with creation of heavens and earth; 17:101–102 soon calls prior signs clear insights. Assigned role: covering suppresses sign-evidence, fragmentation supplies the impossibility-model, and matching recompense returns that chosen closure as experienced result. Abductive move: `بِأَنَّهُمْ` supplies causation; I infer that the punishment matches the epistemic act by making denied reassembly unavoidable. Reading change: the resurrection objection is not incidental speech but the operative model whose rejection of signs structures the recompense.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:99 supplied the decisive correction to the fragmentation model: creation of heavens and earth makes re-proportioning like bodies the smaller analogical case, not an unprecedented operation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P6 (17:97-111): Embodied Inversion and Rekindled Consequence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Rejection reappears as an inverted bodily condition, while exhausted matter and exhausted fire remain subject to renewed formation and intensity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Faculties refused in life become the geometry of resurrection, hell behaves as a fire repeatedly stoked after subsiding, and decayed bodies are measured again under a fixed temporal limit.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Resistant Matter Remade Under a Fixed Term
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Bone and pulverized remains are dispatched into another formation by the same capacity that formed the greater cosmos, with the event fixed to an undisputed term.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: hard bone (`quranic:root_001029:B005/m01`); pulverized fragments (`quranic:root_000578:B001/m01`); dispatch of the raised body (`quranic:root_000129:B002/m01`); originating creation (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); operative capacity (`quranic:root_001205:B003/m01`); fixed term (`quranic:root_000016:B001/m01`); destabilizing doubt (`quranic:root_000616:B001/m01`); refusal (`quranic:root_000008:B001/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The objection again names disintegrated matter, but the answer scales capacity from the larger created field back to the body. The term adds temporal form to material re-formation: neither decay nor uncertainty leaves the event unbounded.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, yapılan bir iyiliğe iyilikle, kötülüğe de kötülükle karşılık vermeyi açıkça ortak çekirdek olarak gösterir. Ödül, olumsuz yaptırım ve öç alma bu iki yönlü karşılık ilişkisinin özel görünümleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca olumlu bir ödülü ya da yalnızca olumsuz bir yaptırımı anlatmaz; karşılığın iki yönünü de kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, genel karşılık verme çekirdeğini korurken belirli kalıplara bağlı hızlı öç alma ve hak edilmiş karşılık kullanımlarını ayrı, bağımlı görünümler olarak tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin yaptığına, iyiyse iyilikle ve kötüyse kötülükle, ona denk ve yeterli bir karşılık vermektir. Ödüllendirme, olumsuz yaptırım ve öç alma bu çekirdeğin yön ya da kullanım bakımından özelleşmiş görünümleridir.

facets.statement: Yapılan eylem, niteliğine uygun ve onu karşılayacak bir iyilik ya da kötülükle yanıtlanır.
Olumlu yönde ödül, olumsuz yönde ise yaptırım ya da öç biçiminde gerçekleşebilir.
Hızlı öç almayı ve övgüye değer işlerle yerine getirilmesi gereken yükümlülüklerin karşılıklarını anlatan özel kullanımlar da bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: جزى يجزي جزاء أي كافأ بالإحسان وبالإساءة (ayn)؛ جزيته بما صنع جزاء وجازيته (sihah)؛ الجزاء يكون ثوابا ويكون عقابا؛ جزيت فلانا بما صنع جزاء؛ جزاء العطاس؛ الجوازي معناها الجزاء (tahdhib)؛ الجزاء ما فيه الكفاية من المقابلة إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر؛ جزيته بكذا وجازيته (mufradat)؛ مكافأته إياه؛ جزيت فلانا أجزيه جزاء وجازيته مجازاة (maqayis)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, bir şeyin ya da kişinin başkasının yerini tutmasını, onun adına işi görmesini ve yeterli olmasını ortak çekirdek olarak verir. İş görme, bir borcu ödeme ve bir edimin sahibi adına yeterli sayılması bu çekirdeğin özel uygulamalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal yapılan işe ödül ya da yaptırım vermeyi değil, başka birinin veya şeyin yerine geçerek yükümlülüğü karşılamayı anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yerini tutma ve yeterli olma çekirdeğini genel biçimde verir; kişi, hayvan, iş, borç ve ödeme kalıplarını bu çekirdeğin ayrı uygulamaları olarak sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin ya da kişinin başkasının yerini tutup onun adına bir işi veya yükümlülüğü karşılaması ve yeterli olmasıdır. İş görme, borç ödeme ve bir edimin sahibi adına yeterli sayılması bu çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşimleridir.

facets.statement: Bir şey ya da kişi başka birinin yerini tutar, onun yerine iş görür ve gereksinimi karşılar.
Bir işin, onu yapması gereken kimse adına tamamlanması yerini tutma çekirdeğinin bir uygulamasıdır.
Birinin alacağını veya borcunu ödemek ya da bir edimin sahibi adına yeterli sayılması da aynı çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yerini tutma ile yeterli olmayı tek yapıda birleştirir; başka biri adına iş görme, ödeme yapma ve yükümlülüğü karşılama bu yapının uygulamalarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin ya da kişinin başkası adına yeterli olması ve gereken işi onun yerine görmesi çekirdeğini anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Yerini tutma, başkası adına iş görme ve yeterli olma bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.text: onun yerine işi görüp yeterli olma
contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişi ya da şeyin başkasının yerini aldığı ve gereken işi karşıladığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Başkasının yerini tutma, onun adına iş görme ve yeterli olma ilişkisini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yerini tutma çekirdeğinin bir alacak veya borç ödemesiyle gerçekleştiği dar bağlamlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Bir yükümlülüğün asıl kişi yerine başkası tarafından karşılanmasını korur.
error_profile.loses: Ödeme dışındaki işlerde yerini tutma ve genel yeterlilik kapsamını dışarıda bırakır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: yeterlilik ve bir işi başkası adına yerine getirme
bu işi benim yerime görüp tamamlama
bir koyunun senin adına yükümlülüğü karşılaması
yeterli olan ve başkasının yerini tutan kimse
birinin alacağını ya da borcunu ödeme

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, yeterli olmanın yanında başkası adına bir işi veya yükümlülüğü yerine getirmeyi de belirginleştirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, yararlı olma ve gereksinimi karşılama yönünü daha genel biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir şeyin ya da kişinin başkasına yeterli olması ve onun yerini tutması iki dalın ortak alanıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda yerini tutarak işi veya yükümlülüğü karşılama yapısaldır; komşu dalın genel yarar ve yeterlilik kapsamı bu uygulamayla sınırlı değildir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalda bir nesne, ödeme ya da edim de başkasının yerini tutabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yalnızca bir kişinin başka bir kişi adına görev üstlenmesine odaklanır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: bir kişinin başkası adına görev yapması
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir kişinin başka birinin yerine geçip onun işini görmesi iki dalda da bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Kişisel görev üstlenme ortak olsa da odak dalın nesne, ödeme ve yeterli sayılan edimlere uzanan kapsamı komşu dalda yoktur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, ödemenin veya edimin başka biri ya da şey adına yeterli olup onun yerini tutmasını gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, alacağın ya da emanetin doğrudan ve eksiksiz biçimde ödenmesine odaklanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir borcun veya ödenmesi gereken şeyin yerine getirilmesi iki dalın kesiştiği alandır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Sırf bir borcu ödemek komşu dala yeter; odak dalda ise ödeme, başka biri adına yeterli sayılma veya onun yerini tutma ilişkisi içinde değerlendirilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, bir şeyin başkası adına yeterli olup onun yerini tutmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, yapılan eylemin iyi ya da kötü bir karşılıkla yanıtlanmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir işin ardından onu karşılayan başka bir edim bulunabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda ikinci edim ilk kişinin yerini tutar veya yükünü karşılar; komşu dalda ise ilk eylemin karşılığıdır ve yerini tutma zorunlu değildir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilen komşular yeterlilik, kişisel görev üstlenme, doğrudan ödeme ve eyleme karşılık verme sınırlarını birbirinden ayırır.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قضاء الشيء عن غيره وقيامه مقامه وكفايته عنه والغناء والحسب وجزاء الحق أو القرض والصدقة التي تجزي عن صاحبها
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو الجزاء بمعنى الثواب والعقاب وحده ولا التقاضي ولا أجزأ المهموز
branches.source_phrase_ar: فلان ذو غناء وجزاء (ayn)؛ جزى عني هذا الأمر أي قضى؛ جزت عنك شاة؛ رجل جازيك أي حسبك (sihah)؛ الجزاء أيضا القضاء؛ لا تقضي فيه نفس عن نفس شيئا؛ جزيت فلانا حقه؛ جزيته قرضه؛ صدقتك جزت عنك؛ هذا رجل حسبك وناهيك وكافيك وجازيك (tahdhib)؛ الجزاء الغناء والكفاية؛ لا يجزي والد عن ولده؛ جازيك فلان أي كافيك (mufradat)؛ قيام الشيء مقام غيره؛ ينوب مناب كل أحد؛ جزى عني هذا الأمر يجزي كما تقول قضى يقضي (maqayis)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, bir borcun ödenmesini borçludan istemeyi ve alacağı elde etmeyi açıkça bildirir; aynı kullanım, bunu yapan kimsenin adlandırılmasını da içerir. Bu nedenle geçici çerçeve kaynakla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal borcu başkası adına ödemeyi değil, borçludan ödemesini istemeyi ve alacağı elde etmeyi anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, borcu isteme kalıbı ile bu işi yapan kişiyi bildiren biçimi ayrı tutar; bunlardan genel bir çıplak kök anlamı çıkarmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir borcun ödenmesini borçludan istemek ve alacağı ondan talep etmektir. Aynı anlam alanı, alacağını isteyen veya borcun ödenmesini talep eden kişi için kullanılan adı da kapsar.

facets.statement: Alacaklı, borçludan borcunu ödemesini ister ve alacağını ondan talep eder.
Borcu isteyen ya da alacağın ödenmesini talep eden kişi bu eyleme bağlı özel bir adla anılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, borçludan ödeme isteme anlamında birleşir ve aynı söz varlığının bu işi yapan kişiyi de adlandırdığını gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir alacaklının borçludan ödeme istemesi veya alacağını talep etmesi anlamındaki kanıtlı bağlamları kapsar.

error_profile.preserves: Borcu isteme, borçluya yönelme ve alacağın ödenmesini talep etme bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Eylemin borçludan ödeme isteme yönünü öne çıkaran bağlamlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Alacaklının borçludan ödeme istemesi ve isteğin borca yönelmesi bileşenlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Alacaklının borçludan alacağını talep ettiği akıcı kullanımlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Alacağı isteme ve talebin borçluya yönelmesi bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: alacağını isteyen veya borcun ödenmesini talep eden kimse

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal özellikle borca yönelir ve borcu isteyen kişi için özel bir adlandırmayı da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, borç dışındaki alacak ve istekleri de kapsar ve istemeyi sürdürme yönünü belirginleştirir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal borç ve onun alınması çevresinde daha sınırlıdır; komşu dal daha geniş alacak türlerine ve isteği sürdürmeye uzanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal yalnızca borçludan ödeme isteme ve alacağı alma yönünü taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal hem borcun ödenmesini hem alacağın istenip alınmasını ve başka ödeme alanlarını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Borcun istenmesi ve alacağın borçludan alınması iki dalda da bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal ödeme yapan tarafın edimini ve daha geniş ödeme türlerini de kapsar; odak dal alacaklının isteme ve alma yönüyle sınırlıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dalda alacaklı, borçludan ödeme ister ve alacağını almaya yönelir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dalda bir kimse borcu öder veya başkası adına yeterli olacak biçimde yükümlülüğü karşılar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal borç ve ödeme çevresinde yer alır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal alacaklının isteme ve alma eylemidir; komşu dal ise ödeme ya da başkası adına yükümlülüğü karşılama eylemidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal borcun ödenmesini isteme ve alacağı elde etme eylemini doğrudan anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal borçlunun oyalaması ile alacaklının buna karşı sürdürdüğü çekişmeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Borçlu ile alacaklı arasındaki ödeme isteme süreci iki dalın ortak alanıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, tarihsel bir yönetim düzeninde koruma statüsü verilen inanç topluluklarından alınan belirli vergiyi açıkça tanımlar. Adın açıklaması konusunda biri yükümlülüğün ödenmesini, diğeri can güvenliği karşılığında yeterli sayılmasını öne çıkaran iki görüş bulunur; ikisi de dalın vergi kimliğini değiştirmez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel vergi ya da herhangi bir pay değildir; belirli bir tarihsel koruma statüsüne bağlı mali yükümlülüktür.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım doğrudan bu tarihsel vergi türünü verir ve kapsamını başka vergi, pay veya genel karşılık anlamlarıyla genişletmez.

concept_map.definition: Tarihsel bir yönetim düzeninde koruma statüsü verilen başka inanç topluluklarından alınan belirli bir vergidir. Adlandırılması, kaynaklarda ya yükümlülüğün ödenmesiyle ya da can güvenliğinin sürmesi karşılığında yeterli sayılmasıyla açıklanır.

facets.statement: Vergi, tarihsel olarak yönetim altında koruma statüsü verilen başka inanç topluluklarından alınır.
Adın gerekçesi, bir açıklamada borç sayılan yükümlülüğün ödenmesine, diğerinde can güvenliği karşılığında yeterli sayılmasına bağlanır.
Sözcüğün çoğul biçimi aynı türdeki vergileri topluca gösterir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar verginin kimliği ve kimlerden alındığı konusunda birleşir; adlandırmayı ise yükümlülüğün ödenmesi veya can güvenliği karşılığında yeterli sayılma üzerinden iki ayrı biçimde açıklar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Belirli bir tarihsel yönetim düzeninde koruma statüsü verilen inanç topluluklarından alınan vergiyi adını ödünç almadan açıklar.

error_profile.preserves: Vergi niteliğini, tarihsel sınırı ve koruma statüsüne bağlı kişi çevresini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tarihsel dönem ve yönetim düzeninin yakın bağlamda belli olduğu açıklayıcı kullanımlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Verginin koruma statüsü verilen topluluklardan alınması yönünü açıkça korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Hangi tarihsel statü ve verginin söz konusu olduğu bağlamdan açıkça anlaşıldığında kısa bir karşılık olarak kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Mali yükümlülük ile özel bir statü arasındaki bağı korur.
error_profile.loses: Verginin hangi topluluklardan ve hangi tarihsel yönetim düzeninde alındığını kendi başına belirtmez.
error_profile.collision: Tek başına kullanıldığında başka statü temelli mali yükümlülüklerle karışabilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Tek kaynak sözü, önce karşılıklı karşılık verme yarışını, ardından konuşanın öteki tarafa üstün gelmesini kuran sabit diziyi açıkça bildirir. Bu nedenle üstün gelme, genel karşılık verme anlamına değil yalnızca bu yapının sonucuna aittir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sıradan karşılık vermeyi değil, karşılıklı karşılık verme içinde yarışıp sonunda üstün gelmeyi anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca verilen karşılıklı eylem dizisine bağlıdır; üstün gelme anlamı çıplak köke veya her karşılık verme kullanımına yayılmaz.

facets.statement: İki taraf karşılıklı olarak birbirine karşılık verir ve anlatılan taraf bu yarışmada ötekine üstün gelir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Bu dal yalnızca belirli bir karşılıklı eylem dizisi içinde değerlendirilir ve genel karşılık verme alanına yayılmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, yapılan işe iyi ya da kötü karşılık vermeyi anlatır ve yarışma sonucu gerektirmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Birleştirilmiş kaynak ifadesi, saçın, yünün ve çeşitli bitkilerin kırkılarak ya da biçilerek kesilmesini ortak çekirdek olarak açıkça destekler. Alet ve yünü kırkılan hayvanlar bu eyleme bağlı adlandırmalardır; ayrı bir eylem çekirdeği oluşturmaz.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, kesme eylemini kapsar; kesim zamanı, kesim ürünü, hurmanın kuruması ve yer adı bu sınırın dışındadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalın kırkıp kesme anlamıyla sınırlıdır ve yalnızca belirli bir söz öbeğine bağlı anlam içermez.

concept_map.definition: Saçı, yünü, otu, ekini veya benzeri bir şeyi kırkarak ya da biçerek kesme eylemidir. Bu eyleme yarayan alet ile yünü kırkılan koyunlar, çekirdeğe bağlı adlandırmalardır.

facets.statement: Saçın, yünün ve benzeri lifli örtülerin kırkılarak kesilmesini anlatır.
Ot, ekin ve ağaç ürünü gibi bitkilerin biçilip kesilmesine de uygulanır.
Kırkma aleti ve yünü kırkılan koyunlar eyleme bağlı adlandırmalar oluşturur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak anlatımı, yün ve saç başta olmak üzere ot, ekin ve ağaç ürünlerinin kırkılıp kesilmesini; ayrıca kullanılan aleti ve yünü alınan koyunları kapsar.

concept_gloss.text: saç, yün veya bitkiyi kırkıp kesme

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem kırkım, hasat veya toplama zamanını adlandıran biçimi hem de ekin, ağaç ürünü, koyun ya da topluluk için bu zamanın geldiğini bildiren türemiş kullanımları bir arada verir. Dalın zaman ve hazır oluş çerçevesi bu iki katmanı doğru biçimde korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Burada odak kesme eylemi değil, kesim için uygun vaktin veya hazır oluş aşamasının gelmesidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, zaman bildiren adlandırmayı kesime hazır oluş bildiren türemiş kullanımlardan ayırır ve bunları yalın kesme anlamıyla birleştirmez.

concept_map.definition: Kırkım, biçim veya ürün toplama vaktini ve bir hayvanın, bitkinin ya da topluluğun bu iş için uygun zamana ulaşmasını anlatır. Zamanın adı ile hazır oluşu bildiren kullanımlar aynı dalda fakat ayrı katmanlardır.

facets.statement: Kırkma, hasat etme veya ağaç ürününü toplama zamanını adlandırır.
Ekinin, ağacın veya koyunun kesim ya da kırkım vaktine ulaştığını bildirir.
Bir topluluğun hayvanlarını kırkma veya ekinini biçme vaktinin gelmesine de aktarılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar kırkım ve hasat vaktini, ekin ile ağaç ürününün kesime hazır oluşunu ve bir topluluğun hayvanlarını ya da ekinini işleme zamanının gelmesini birlikte aktarır.

concept_gloss.text: kesim ya da hasat vaktinin gelmesi

error_profile.preserves: Uygun zamanı ve o zamana ulaşma durumunu birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kırkıldıktan sonra henüz kullanılmamış yünü, bir koyundan alınan yünü, bir tutam yünü ve deri ya da başka bir şey kesildiğinde düşen parçayı aynı sonuç ve artık alanında toplar. Dal çerçevesi eylemi değil, eylemin ürününü veya kalıntısını doğru biçimde merkez alır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Kırkma eylemi ile kırkım zamanı dışarıdadır; burada yeni alınmış yün ve kesimden kalan parça söz konusudur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalın kesim ürünü ve artığı alanını korur; süs amacıyla asılan yün parçalarını bu çekirdeğe katmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kırkma sonucunda elde edilen ve henüz kullanılmamış yünü ya da bir koyundan alınan yün miktarını anlatır. Ayrıca deri veya başka bir şey kesildiğinde düşen ya da fazla kalan parçayı kapsar.

facets.statement: Kırkıldıktan sonra henüz kullanılmamış yünü anlatır.
Bir koyundan alınan yün miktarını veya tek bir yün tutamını adlandırır.
Deri ya da başka bir şey kesildiğinde düşen veya fazla kalan parçaya uzanır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الصوف المجزوز الذي لم يستعمل، جزة الشاة، خصلة الصوف أو الجزيزة، والجزازة لما يسقط من الأديم وغيره إذا قطع

branches.source_phrase_ar: الجزيزة خصلة من صوف والجمع جزائز والجزازة ما سقط من الأديم (maqayis); الجزز الصوف الذي لم يستعمل بعد ما جز وصوف كل شاة جزة والجزاز ما فضل من الأديم (ayn); الجزة صوف شاة والجزازة ما سقط من الأديم والجزيزة خصلة من الصوف (sihah); الجزز الصوف الذي لم يستعمل بعدما جز وهذه جزة هذه الشاة والجزاز ما فضل من الأديم (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ortak ağırlığı, deve sırtındaki yolcu bölmesine bağlanan veya asılan boyalı yün tutamlarındadır.
